title: apps/alerting/rules — what must change together when extending kinds/validation
answers: What breaks if I add a new field/kind to apps/alerting/rules without updating the manifest?
Where do I register a new RuntimeConfig field?
Do AlertRule and RecordingRule share validation logic?
What must stay consistent with RuleSequence membership refs?
body:
1. Field/kind changes start in `apps/alerting/rules/kinds/v0alpha1/*.cue`, run through `make generate` (app-sdk generate). A new kind additionally needs an entry in `apps/alerting/rules/kinds/manifest.cue` and in `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/apis/types.go:GetKinds`, plus a `case` arm in the `switch kind.Kind()` inside `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/app.go:buildKindValidator`/`buildKindMutator`. Missing the manifest entry fails `ValidateManifest` at startup.
2. AlertRule and RecordingRule validators are intentionally duplicated, not shared — compare `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/alertrule/validator.go` vs `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/recordingrule/validator.go`. Only genuinely cross-kind logic is factored into `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/util/` (`ValidateGroupLabels`, `ValidateInterval`, `ValidateExpressions`). A kind-specific rule change must be applied to both files manually; `util` changes affect both.
3. RuleSequence membership spans the spec, the validator, and the index: if ref storage in `RuleSequenceSpec` changes, `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/rulesequence/membership_index.go` (`collectRuleUIDs`) must change too or the index silently drops/misattributes refs; `rulesequence/validator.go` consumes `config.RuleSequenceMembershipResolver`.
4. Any new `config.RuntimeConfig` field (`apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/config/runtime.go`) needs a real implementation added in `pkg/registry/apps/alerting/rules/register.go` (the `rulesAppConfig.RuntimeConfig{...}` literal) AND a fake value in `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/app_test.go` (RuntimeConfig builder for tests), or tests fail to compile/exercise the new field.
5. A nil `*simple.Validator`/`*simple.Mutator` assigned into an interface-typed field in `app.go:New` is explicitly guarded against — assigning a nil pointer via a non-nil interface makes `ValidateManifest` think a kind (e.g. Config) has a validator/mutator it doesn't; always check `if validator != nil` before assigning.
applies: Applies when adding/changing a kind, a validator rule, RuleSequence membership refs, or RuntimeConfig fields in apps/alerting/rules; not relevant to ngalert evaluation/storage code outside this app.
